display.title: The Haggadah Explained in Yiddish: The Four Sons to Vayered Mitzraymah (Excerpt)
display.summary_short: An excerpt of the Yiddish Haggadah class for children: the Four Sons with a teaching of the Rebbe, Mitchilah, V'hi She'amdah and Arami Oved Avi.
display.summary_long: Told in Yiddish for children, this excerpt from the middle of a Haggadah class opens with Baruch HaMakom and the Four Sons: the Torah has an answer for every kind of child. The teacher shares the Rebbe's teaching on why the rasha is placed right after the chacham, so that the wise son reaches out to him, since the 'echad' of Hashem Echad is hidden in every Jew. He explains each son's question and answer, then Yachol meRosh Chodesh, why the story is told only when matzah and maror are on the table. Next come Mitchilah, our ancestors before Avraham Avinu, and Hashem's promise at the Bris Bein HaBesarim, followed by how to cover the matzah and hold the cup for V'hi She'amdah, which is sung. It ends with Tzei U'lmad about Lavan and the first verse of Arami Oved Avi: how Yaakov's family went down to Egypt meaning to stay only a short time, and how the Jews remained a distinct people there.
display.lesson: Every kind of child deserves an answer, and even the rasha has a hidden spark that a caring Jew can reveal.

advisories.note: Lavan's plan against Yaakov's family, Pharaoh's decree, and enemies who rise up in every generation.
